events.summary:
TORAMA

The National Weather Service in Amarillo has issued a

* Tornado Warning for...
Northwestern Texas County in the panhandle of Oklahoma...

* Until 1230 AM CST.

* At 1155 PM CST, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing a
tornado was located 6 miles north of Eva, or 29 miles northwest of
Guymon, moving northeast at 45 mph.

HAZARD...Tornado.

SOURCE...Radar indicated rotation.

IMPACT...Flying debris will be dangerous to those caught without
shelter. Mobile homes will be damaged or destroyed. Damage
to roofs, windows and vehicles will occur. Tree damage is
likely.

* Locations impacted include...
Eva.

events.summary:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

San Francisco River at Reserve affecting Catron County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...San Francisco River at Reserve.

* WHEN...Until Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 16.5 feet, Water will begin to over top the berm on
the right bank (south side) and impact residences. Water will begin
to impact commercial land on the left bank (north side) of the
river. Low spots on The Lane may be impacted. Low spots on the
north side of Highway 12 may see flooding.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:10 PM MST Sunday the stage was 12.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 13.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
tomorrow morning and continue falling to 15.8 feet late this
evening. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 15.0 feet.
- Flood History...No available flood history.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.summary:
...The National Weather Service in Tucson has issued a Flood Warning
for the following rivers in Arizona...

Gila River Near Gila River near Solomon affecting Graham County.

For the Upper Gila...including Gila River near Solomon...Major
flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is forecast.


* WHERE...Gila River near Solomon.


* WHEN...Until Monday evening.


* IMPACTS...At 24.0 feet, Several homes and businesses may become
flooded, mostly on the north side of Solomon, Safford, and
Thatcher. Bridges may be over-topped.


* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:15 PM MST Sunday the stage was 18.4 feet.

- Bankfull stage is 19.0 feet.

- Forecast...The river will rise above flood stage late this
evening to 26.9 feet around daybreak. It will continue to rise to
28.4 feet late tomorrow morning. It will then fall below flood
stage to 19.8 feet early Tuesday morning.

- Flood stage is 21.0 feet.

- Flood History...This historical peak crest of 42.8 feet was
observed on 10/02/1983.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Castle Country; San Rafael Swell; Lower Washington County; Zion National Park; Southern Mountains; Bryce Canyon Country; South Central Utah; Capitol Reef National Park and Vicinity; Western Canyonlands; Glen Canyon Recreation Area/Lake Powell
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
The Flood Watch will expire for a portion of Utah, including the
following areas, Castle Country, San Rafael Swell, Bryce Canyon
Country, Capitol Reef National Park and Vicinity, Glen Canyon
Recreation Area/Lake Powell, South Central Utah, Southern Mountains,
Western Canyonlands, Lower Washington County and Zion National Park.

Current flood warnings remain in effect for Zion NP, the Paria River,
and interests along the Escalante River. However, rainfall continues
to taper off elsewhere with no new flooding expected outside of the
previously mentioned locations. Therefore, the Flood Watch will
expire at 11 PM MST this evening.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Upper Rio Grande Valley/Eastern San Juan Mountains Below 10000 Ft; Eastern San Juan Mountains Above 10000 Ft
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected to occur.

* WHERE...Eastern San Juan Mountains Above 10000 Feet, Upper Rio
Grande Valley and Eastern San Juan Mountains Below 10000 Feet.

* WHEN...Through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone location.
Rockslides will be possible in the mountainous areas. Highway 160
and Highway 17 will likely be significantly impacted by this storm.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Heavy rainfall is expected to fall through Monday across the
area, leading to elevated concerns for flooding in areas that
have recently received excessive moisture, or have recently
experienced flooding.
- The greatest risk of flooding will be along the Conejos River and
the South Fork of the Rio Grande, including South Fork and
Mogote.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood http://cotrip.org

events.region: Del Norte Vicinity/Northern San Luis Valley Below 8500 Ft; Alamosa  Vicinity/Central San Luis Valley Below 8500 Ft; Southern San Luis Valley
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall will be possible,
especially over the western half of San Luis Valley.

* WHERE...The western half of the San Luis Valley, including
Antonito, Del Norte, Monte Vista and Alamosa.

* WHEN...Through late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone location.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Runoff from heavy rain and melting snow over the San Juan
Mountains may cause flooding in the San Luis Valley, especially
Monday and Tuesday as high flows move out of the mountains and
through the Rio Grande and Conejos River.
- The greatest risk of flooding will be along the Conejos River and
the Rio Grande, including Del Norte, Monte Vista and Alamosa.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood http://cotrip.org
